description:
Programme or Project Overview

The Department of Peace and Conflict Research at Uppsala University invites applications for two PhD candidates within the DIViNE doctoral network, a Marie Sklodowska-Curie Actions project on political violence and democracy. The advertised projects address institutional reform and public support for political violence, asking how institutional change shapes citizens' attitudes toward violent and democratic political action. The department hosts the Uppsala Conflict Data Program (UCDP), one of the world's leading data resources on organised violence, giving doctoral candidates direct access to exceptional data and expertise.

Each position is a salaried doctoral appointment under the Swedish collective agreement, embedded in an international network of partner universities and research organisations. DIViNE doctoral candidates follow joint training, participate in network workshops and secondments, and contribute to comparative research on how political violence emerges, persists and declines in democratic settings. The positions suit candidates aiming for a research career in conflict studies, political science or policy analysis.

Candidate profile

Applicants hold a master's degree in peace and conflict research, political science or a closely related social-science discipline, with strong quantitative or mixed-methods skills and an interest in institutions, violence and democratic attitudes. Experience with survey data, conflict datasets or comparative analysis is an advantage. Applications are submitted through Uppsala University's Varbi system with a CV, transcripts, references, a statement of research interests and any written work the applicant wishes to highlight.

Highlights

  • Two PhD positions in the DIViNE MSCA doctoral network
  • Department of Peace and Conflict Research, home of UCDP
  • Institutional reform and public support for political violence
  • Salaried four-year doctoral employment
  • Network workshops, training and secondments
  • World-leading conflict data environment
